2607.04436.title: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Detecting and Resolving Pragmatic Ambiguities in Natural Language Requirements
2607.04436.paper_summary: Natural language requirements (NLRs) are essential for bridging communication gaps among diverse stakeholders in software development. However, the inherent ambiguity in NLRs can pose significant challenges. In particular, some requirements may be misinterpreted due to varying contextual knowledge and domain-specific expectations of the stakeholders, a phenomenon known as pragmatic ambiguity. This paper presents an approach for detecting and resolving pragmatic ambiguities in NLRs. The approach leverages retrieval-augmented generation techniques with novice, intermediate, and expert domain knowledge bases to simulate stakeholders with varying domain expertise and detect discrepancies in requirement interpretation. Candidate disambiguated requirements are generated using the expert domain knowledge base, with final validation by a requirements analyst required to ensure alignment with the intended functionality. We evaluate the approach on two requirements specification documents from the PUblic REquirements dataset, using four large language models: GPT-4o-mini, Mistral-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Detection performance is assessed using macro-averaged accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and F2 scores. The resolution quality of the candidate disambiguated requirements is measured through human evaluation of relevance, clarity, and consistency. In this initial evaluation, results show that the proposed approach can detect pragmatic ambiguities and produce candidate disambiguated requirements that are relevant, clear, and consistent with the intended system functionality. Among the evaluated models, GPT-4o-mini achieved the highest macro-averaged recall (0.75) and F2 score (0.75) for pragmatic ambiguity detection. In the resolution task, GPT-4o-mini received the highest relevance scores from human evaluators, while Mistral-7B achieved the highest scores for clarity and consistency.
2607.04436.paper_summary_zh: 自然語言需求（NLRs）對於彌合軟體開發中不同利益相關者之間的溝通差距至關重要。<lb/>然而，NLRs固有的模糊性可能會帶來重大挑戰。<lb/>特別是，由於利益相關者的上下文知識和特定領域期望的差異，一些需求可能會被誤解，這種現象被稱為實用模糊性。<lb/>本文提出了一種檢測和解決NLRs中實用模糊性的方法。<lb/>該方法利用增強檢索生成技術，結合新手、中級和專家領域知識庫，以模擬擁有不同領域專業知識的利益相關者並檢測需求解釋中的差異。<lb/>候選的消歧義需求是使用專家領域知識庫生成的，最終需要由需求分析師進行驗證，以確保與預期功能的一致性。<lb/>我們在PUblic REquirements數據集的兩份需求規範文件上評估了該方法，使用四個大型語言模型：GPT-4o-mini、Mistral-7B、Llama-3.1-8B和Qwen2.5-7B。<lb/>檢測性能使用宏平均準確率、精確率、召回率、F1和F2分數進行評估。<lb/>候選消歧義需求的解決質量通過人類對相關性、清晰性和一致性的評估來衡量。<lb/>在這次初步評估中，結果顯示所提出的方法可以檢測實用模糊性並產生與預期系統功能相關、清晰且一致的候選消歧義需求。<lb/>在評估的模型中，GPT-4o-mini在實用模糊性檢測中達到了最高的宏平均召回率（0.75）和F2分數（0.75）。<lb/>在解決任務中，GPT-4o-mini從人類評估者那裡獲得了最高的相關性分數，而Mistral-7B在清晰性和一致性方面則獲得了最高分數。
